CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough for one week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 74-year-old male who reports that his cough started approximately one week ago. He has been bringing up yellow sputum and reports feeling worse over the last two days. He denies fever but reports feeling warm. He denies chills but endorses feeling achy at times. He denies shortness of breath. He reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and some sinus pressure. Additionally, the patient reports that while coughing earlier today, he fell down approximately four to five stairs and twisted his right knee. He is able to walk but reports pain mostly on the inside of the knee with a mild limp. He has not taken any pain medication for the knee but has been taking over-the-counter Dayquil for his cough and cold symptoms, which has provided minimal relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for cough with yellow sputum, nasal congestion, postnasal drainage, sinus pressure, general achiness, and right knee pain. Denies fever, chills, shortness of breath, or knee giving out.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension. Diabetes.

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Metformin 1000 milligrams twice daily. Over-the-counter Dayquil.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a teacher. Lives with his wife. No one else in the household is sick.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62, Heart Rate 80s, Oxygen Saturation 97% on room air. Facial Exam: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses. Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of bilateral nasal turbinates with yellow discharge. Throat Exam: Uvula midline, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space. Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy. Lung Exam: Coarse rhonchi bilateral that clears with cough. Heart Exam: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmur. Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation on right medial knee, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to right medial knee, no effusion.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis: Continue over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 milligrams twice daily. No antibiotics at this time. Patient to call if symptoms worsen; will consider chest x-ray to rule out pneumonia.
2. Right medial collateral ligament strain: Prescribe meloxicam 15 milligrams once daily. Refer to physical therapy. Order right knee x-ray to rule out bone injury.
3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 milligrams daily. Order lipid panel.
4. Diabetes: Order hemoglobin A1c. Encouraged patient to monitor sugar intake and report blood sugars through patient portal. Counseled regarding importance of diet monitoring to prevent complications such as kidney dysfunction and eye problems.
